# Model the review page's mutually-exclusive UI state as ADTs

## Problem

In the bank-statement review page components, two bits of UI state are encoded
as several parallel `useState`s where at most one case can hold and setting one
must clear the others — the pattern `.orca/reviewers/frontend.md` now flags.
Replace each with a single ADT (`enum`/sealed type) held in one `useState`, so
illegal combinations are unrepresentable and each transition is one assignment.

This is a **pure, behaviour-preserving refactor** — identical UI and behaviour.

## 1. Drawer form state

`BankStatementReviewContent.scala` holds four `Option[UUID]`s for which drawer
form is open:

```
creatingForRow, linkingForRow, creatingRefundForRow, ruleFormForRow
```

At most one is ever `Some`; opening one clears the others (today via the
`activeForm`/open-drawer logic). Replace them with one state, e.g.:

```scala
enum DrawerState:
  case Closed
  case CreateExpense(rowId: UUID)
  case CreateRefund(rowId: UUID)
  case LinkExpense(rowId: UUID)
  case CreateRule(rowId: UUID)
```

held in a single `useState[DrawerState]`. Opening a form is one assignment;
closing is `Closed`; "is the drawer open" is `!= Closed`. Update the row-action
handlers, the `activeForm`-style helpers (fold them into the ADT / its home in
`BankStatementReviewLogic`), and the `BankStatementReviewDrawer` props to take
the `DrawerState` (or the resolved case) instead of four options.

## 2. Bulk-run state

`BankStatementReviewPage.scala` holds two progress/results pairs — one per bulk
run (ignore, import):

```
bulkIgnoreProgress + bulkIgnoreResults
bulkImportProgress + bulkImportResults   // BulkProgress = Option[(Int,Int,Int)], BulkResults = List[...]
```

Each pair is one `Idle → Running → Done` machine split across two fields that can
drift (progress `None` while results non-empty). Replace each pair with one ADT,
shared by both runs:

```scala
enum BulkRun:
  case Idle
  case Running(done: Int, total: Int, failed: Int)
  case Done(results: List[(UUID, Either[String, Unit])])
```

so there is one `useState[BulkRun]` per run. Update the bulk handlers
(`handleBulkIgnore`, `handleBulkImport` and their loops) to advance the single
state, and `BankStatementBulkRuns` (which renders this) to read it. Keep the
rendered output and messages identical.

## Constraints

- Behaviour-preserving: same drawer open/close behaviour, same bulk progress
  display, counts, toasts, and result summaries. No API/server/styling changes.
- Follow `.orca/reviewers/frontend.md` (the new rule) and the project's frontend
  conventions (`FunctionalComponent`/`Props`, `val` only for plain JS literals,
  `def` for reused React elements, MUI callbacks via `(opt: Any) match`).
- Scope: the review-page components only
  (`BankStatementReview*`, `BankStatementBulkRuns`, `BankStatementRowActions`,
  and `BankStatementReviewLogic`). Do not touch other pages.
- Tests stay green and move/extend with the code (`BankStatementReviewLogicSpec`,
  `BankStatementBulkRunsSpec`); `web/Test/compile` passes.

## Out of scope

- No change to what the drawer forms or bulk runs actually do, to matching, or
  to any fetch.
- Other pages that may share the pattern — not in this task.

## Acceptance

- The four drawer `Option[UUID]`s are replaced by one `DrawerState` value; the
  two progress/results pairs by one `BulkRun` value each; no parallel flag is
  reset in groups any more.
- The page behaves exactly as before; web compiles and all web tests pass.

resultJson.description:
The bank-statement review page keeps two pieces of UI state in parallel `Hooks.useState`s where only one case can be true at a time. That is the pattern `.orca/reviewers/frontend.md` now flags. First, `BankStatementReviewContent` tracks which drawer form is open with four `Option[UUID]`s (`creatingForRow`, `linkingForRow`, `creatingRefundForRow`, `ruleFormForRow`). It closes them in groups and needs a precedence helper (`BankStatementReviewDrawer.activeForm`) to work out which one wins. Second, `BankStatementReviewPage` tracks each bulk run (ignore, import) as a `BulkProgress` (`Option[(done,total,failed)]`) plus a `BulkResults` list. Each pair is really one Idle → Running → Done machine, but the two halves can drift apart. This epic replaces each with a single ADT in a single `useState`: `DrawerState` (Closed | CreateExpense | CreateRefund | LinkExpense | CreateRule, each carrying `rowId`) and `BulkRun` (Idle | Running | Done). After this, impossible combinations can't be represented, and every transition is one assignment or one functional update.

This is a pure refactor that must not change behaviour. The drawer's open/close behaviour, the bulk bar's "Processing d/t (f failed)…" and "Ignoring d/t…" labels, the button enabling, the toasts, and the results list must all stay the same. The pure parts (the ADTs and their transition and query helpers) go in `BankStatementReviewLogic` and are tested in `BankStatementReviewLogicSpec`. The bulk loops stay in `BankStatementBulkRuns`, and `BankStatementBulkRunsSpec` asserts the new single-state sequence. Nothing changes in API, server, styling or other pages.

One deliberate deviation from the sketch in the issue: `BulkRun.Running` must also carry the results collected so far. Today the results list fills in row by row while the run is still going: `BankStatementReviewBulkResults` renders whenever any results exist, including mid-run. A `Running(done,total,failed)` with no results would drop that display. Every loop step adds exactly one result, and failed is exactly the number of `Left`s. So the drift-free version is `Running(total: Int, results: BulkResults)`, with `done = results.size` and `failed = results.count(_.isLeft)` derived from it.

tasks.title: Replace the four drawer Option[UUID]s with one DrawerState ADT
tasks.description:
Add `enum DrawerState { case Closed; case CreateExpense(rowId: UUID); case CreateRefund(rowId: UUID); case LinkExpense(rowId: UUID); case CreateRule(rowId: UUID) }` to `BankStatementReviewLogic`. Give it a small pure helper such as `def rowId: Option[UUID]` (None for Closed), plus a pure "close only if this form is still the one showing" transition, e.g. `def closing(form: DrawerState): DrawerState = if (this == form) Closed else this`.

In `BankStatementReviewContent`:
- Replace the four `Option[UUID]` useStates with `val (drawerState, setDrawerState) = Hooks.useState[DrawerState](DrawerState.Closed)`.
- In `onRowAction`, each Open* case becomes one assignment (`setDrawerState(DrawerState.CreateExpense(rowId))`, and so on). The callback's deps stay unchanged.
- `drawerOpen` becomes `drawerState != DrawerState.Closed`.
- Resolve the row with `drawerState.rowId.flatMap(id => statementRows.find(_.id == id))`.
- `closeDrawer` becomes `setDrawerState(DrawerState.Closed)`.
- The success callbacks (expense created/linked, refund created, rule created) and the per-form cancel close through a functional update: `setDrawerState(_.closing(<that form's state>))`.

In `BankStatementReviewDrawer`:
- Remove `activeForm` and the `DrawerForm` enum.
- Change Props to take `state: DrawerState` and `row: Option[StatementRowData]` instead of `open` and `target`, with `open = state != Closed`.
- `renderForm` matches on the DrawerState case.
- `onCancel` takes the `DrawerState` being cancelled, or is dropped in favour of a close callback if that is cleaner while keeping the same behaviour.

Tests: delete `BankStatementReviewDrawerSpec`, since `activeForm` no longer exists, and add a `DrawerState` section to `BankStatementReviewLogicSpec` covering `rowId` for each case and the `closing` semantics (closes when equal, leaves another open form alone). Verify with `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile` and `sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewLogicSpec"`.

tasks.title: Replace each bulk progress+results pair with one BulkRun ADT
tasks.description:
Add `enum BulkRun { case Idle; case Running(total: Int, results: BulkResults); case Done(results: BulkResults) }` to `BankStatementReviewLogic`. `Running` carries its results so the mid-run results list keeps rendering. Pure helpers:
- `results: BulkResults` (Idle → Nil)
- `isRunning: Boolean`
- on Running, `done = results.size` and `failed = results.count(_.isLeft)`
- `recorded(rowId: UUID, outcome: Either[String, Unit]): BulkRun` (appends while Running, otherwise unchanged)
- `finished: BulkRun` (Running(_, rs) → Done(rs), otherwise unchanged)

Remove the `BulkProgress` alias. Keep `BulkResults`, since `BankStatementReviewBulkResults` uses it.

In `BankStatementReviewPage`, replace the four useStates with `val (bulkIgnore, setBulkIgnore) = Hooks.useState[BulkRun](BulkRun.Idle)` and the same for `bulkImport`. Keep them in the page with the existing comment: they must survive the remount a refresh causes. Thread them through `BankStatementReviewContent.Props` as `bulkIgnore`/`setBulkIgnore`/`bulkImport`/`setBulkImport`, replacing the eight fields.

In `BankStatementBulkRuns`, `handleBulkIgnore` and `handleBulkImport` each take one `SetStateHookCallback[BulkRun]`:
- on start: `set(BulkRun.Running(total, Nil))`
- per row: `set(_.recorded(rowId, outcome))`, as one functional update in place of the separate results and progress updates
- at the end: `set(_.finished)`, before clearing the selection and, for import, the toast and `onRefresh`, in the same order as today

The import loop's `Counts` stays as it is for the summary toast.

In `BankStatementReviewContent`:
- `bulkActive = selectedInView.nonEmpty && !bulkIgnore.isRunning && !bulkImport.isRunning`
- the results section renders when `(bulkImport.results ++ bulkIgnore.results).nonEmpty`, passing that concatenation in the same order as today

`BankStatementReviewBulkBar` Props take `importRun: BulkRun` / `ignoreRun: BulkRun` and match `case r: BulkRun.Running` to show the same "Processing $done/$total( ($failed failed))…" and "Ignoring …" text, falling back to the existing buttons otherwise.

Tests:
- Update `BankStatementBulkRunsSpec` to record a single `Recorder[BulkRun]`. The ignore test expects states `Running(2,Nil)`, `Running(2,[ok→Right])`, `Running(2,[ok→Right, bad→Left(boom)])`, `Done(same)`. The import tests make the equivalent assertions, and the toast event captures `Done(...)` rather than `None`.
- Add `BulkRun` helper tests (recorded, finished, done/failed derivation, results on Idle) to `BankStatementReviewLogicSpec`.

Verify with `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile`, `sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementBulkRunsSpec"` and `sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewLogicSpec"`.

resultJson.brief:
Module: `web/` (Scala 3, Scala.js + Slinky React + MUI 5 via `com.olvind.mui.muiMaterial.components as mui`). All files are in `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/`, with tests in `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/`. The rule being applied is in `.orca/reviewers/frontend.md`: mutually-exclusive UI state should be one enum held in one `useState`, and no handler should reset sibling states in groups.

Files:
- `BankStatementReviewLogic.scala`: pure logic, no React or MUI. Defines `type BulkProgress = Option[(Int,Int,Int)]` (done,total,failed), `type BulkResults = List[(UUID, Either[String, Unit])]`, and `RowEdits`, plus existing Scala 3 enums written with braces (`enum LinkedCategory { case ... }`, `RowMenuItem`, `PrimaryAction`, `BulkRowDecision`). New ADTs go here in the same brace style, with scaladoc comments like their neighbours. Other files use it via `import BankStatementReviewLogic.*`.
- `BankStatementReviewPage.scala`: holds `toast` and the four bulk useStates. They live here, not in the content, so they survive the `withKey(timesRefreshing)` remount on refresh. The page renders `AsyncComponent[ReviewData]` → `BankStatementReviewContent`.
- `BankStatementReviewContent.scala`: the main body. It holds the drawer state (four `Option[UUID]`s at ~L78-81) and copies the bulk props into locals (L48-55).
  - `onRowAction` is a `Hooks.useCallback` with deps `List(stmtId.toString)`. It may only use stable setters (useState setters are stable).
  - Open-form handlers today: OpenExpenseForm sets creating and clears linking, OpenLinkPicker sets linking and clears creating, OpenRefundForm/OpenRuleForm set only their own.
  - Other drawer logic: `drawerOpen` is the OR of the four options, `drawerTarget` comes from `activeForm` plus `statementRows.find`, `closeDrawer` clears all four, and each per-form `onCancel` or success callback clears only its own option.
  - Bulk: `bulkActive` (L162) requires both progresses to be None. The results section (L262) renders `bulkImportResults ++ bulkIgnoreResults` whenever it is non-empty, which includes mid-run.
- `BankStatementReviewDrawer.scala`: `enum DrawerForm` + `activeForm(creating, refund, linking, rule): Option[(UUID, DrawerForm)]` (precedence creating > refund > linking > rule). Props: `open: Boolean`, `target: Option[(StatementRowData, DrawerForm)]`, `onClose`, `onCancel: DrawerForm => Unit`, `onExpenseCreated/onRefundCreated/onExpenseLinked: (UUID,UUID)=>Unit`, `onRuleCreated`, `onNewEntities`. `renderForm` builds `BankRowCreateExpenseForm` / `BankRowCreateRefundForm` / `BankRowLinkPicker` / `BankRowRuleForm`. The MUI Drawer is the temporary (modal) variant, so row buttons can't be clicked while it is open. That means the "two options set at once" states are unreachable in practice, and a single ADT is equivalent for every reachable state. `activeForm` is only used by Content and `BankStatementReviewDrawerSpec`.
- `BankStatementBulkRuns.scala`: not a component.
  - `handleBulkIgnore(client, stmtId, ids, setStatementRows, setBulkIgnoreProgress, setBulkIgnoreResults, setSelectedRowIds)(implicit ec)`. It sets progress to `Some((0,total,0))` and results to `Nil`, then per row appends a result via functional update and sets progress to `Some((done+1,total,failed'))`; at the end it sets progress to None and clears the selection.
  - `handleBulkImport(...)` has the same shape plus `Counts(linked,created,ignored,failed)`, with `advance(outcome, next, nextLinked)` doing the two sets. At the end: progress None → `setSelectedRowIds(Set.empty)` → `showToast(bulkImportSummary(...))` → `onRefresh()`.
  - Invariant: done == number of results and failed == number of `Left`s, so the derived `done`/`failed` on `Running` are exact.
  - Results are not cleared at the end (they stay displayed), and starting one run doesn't clear the other run's results.
- `BankStatementReviewBulkBar.scala`: Props `importProgress: BulkProgress, ignoreProgress: BulkProgress`, matched as `Some((done,total,failed))` to show the text `s"Processing $done/$total${if (failed > 0) s" ($failed failed)" else ""}…"` (and the same with "Ignoring"); otherwise it shows the "Process ready"/"Ignore" buttons, disabled when `!bulkActive`. Keep the strings byte-identical.
- `BankStatementReviewBulkResults.scala`: `Props(results: BulkResults, descById)`. No change is needed.
- `BankStatementRowActions.scala`: single-row API actions. It touches no drawer or bulk state, so it probably needs no change.

Tests:
- `BankStatementBulkRunsSpec`: uses a `Recorder[T]` that wraps `SetStateHookCallback[T]` and applies function updaters like React (`js.typeOf(arg) == "function"`). It records `states` and `value`. `StubClient extends ApiClient` overrides ignoreRow/linkRowToExpense/createExpenseFromRow. `ExecutionContext.parasitic` makes the loops run synchronously. Its assertions on the progress `states` list must become assertions on the `BulkRun` state sequence.
- `BankStatementReviewLogicSpec`: AnyWordSpec + `must` matchers, `"thing" should { "..." in {...} }`.
- `BankStatementReviewDrawerSpec`: only tests `activeForm`.

Conventions:
- Components are `object X { def apply(props: Props): KeyAddingStage = component(props); case class Props(...); val component = FunctionalComponent[Props] { ... } }`.
- Object-level `val`s may only be plain JS literals or styles. Use `def` for reused React elements. MUI callbacks follow the `(opt: Any) match` idiom.
- Advance state with functional updates (`setX(cur => ...)`) inside async loops, so updates from earlier rows aren't lost.
- Keep changes surgical and match the surrounding comment density.
- Format with scalafmt (`sbt scalafmtAll`).
- Verify only with targeted runs: `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile` and `sbt "web/testOnly *<Spec>"`, never the full `sbt test`.
- Web tests need Node 24 on PATH (the default shell node is v16, and yarn install fails on it).

The full suite passes: `CI=true NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider sbt test` exited with code 0 on the first run, so I changed no code.

- **Results:** every module reported 0 failures. Server: 876 tests, web: 295, plus smaller modules (36 and 56 tests).
- **Setup:** Docker was already running, so testcontainers started its own Postgres. I ran it with Node v24.15.0, which accepts `--openssl-legacy-provider`.
- **Error lines in the log:** a few "Failed…" and stack-trace lines (e.g. `BackgroundJobTypeRunnerSpec`'s "claim boom" / "record boom") are failures the tests trigger on purpose, not test failures.

The full log is at `/tmp/fulltest.log`.

resultJson.title: Model review page drawer and bulk-run state as ADTs
resultJson.body:
The bank-statement review page kept two pieces of UI state in parallel `useState`s, where only one case can be true at a time. This is the pattern `.orca/reviewers/frontend.md` flags. This PR puts each one in a single ADT in `BankStatementReviewLogic`. It's a refactor only: the UI and behaviour are meant to stay the same.

- **Drawer:** the four `Option[UUID]`s in `BankStatementReviewContent` are now one `DrawerState` (`Closed | CreateExpense | CreateRefund | LinkExpense | CreateRule`). This removes `activeForm`, `DrawerForm` and `BankStatementReviewDrawerSpec`. The drawer gets a single `target: Option[(row, DrawerState)]` and no longer takes a separate `open` flag. Cancel and success callbacks close the drawer with `_.closing(form)`, which only closes it if that form is still the one open. `onRuleCreated` now also receives the row id so it can do this.
- **Bulk runs:** each progress/results pair in `BankStatementReviewPage` is now one `BulkRun` (`Idle | Running | Done`) per run. `handleBulkIgnore` and `handleBulkImport` now move this one state forward. The bulk bar reads it, and the "Processing…" / "Ignoring…" text is unchanged.

One deliberate difference from the sketch in the task: `Running` is `Running(total, results)`, not `Running(done, total, failed)`. Today the results list fills in row by row while a run is still going, and dropping the results from `Running` would lose that. `done` and `failed` are now worked out from the results (`results.size`, and the count of `Left`s), so they can't drift.

`BankStatementBulkRunsSpec` now checks the sequence of `BulkRun` states. `BankStatementReviewLogicSpec` covers the `DrawerState` and `BulkRun` helpers.
